It says generically that voltage, discharge current, BMS and charger must be 'compatible with your golf cart', but it never mentions the Club Car OBC, which brand-specific kit to buy, or Redodo's stated ban on using its 12V packs in golf carts. The OBC point decides whether an older Club Car will charge after the swap. It doesn't change which product to buy (both kits use a separate 58.4V lithium charger), so it rates 2, not 3.
kit_items: 48V LiFePO4 battery + matched charger + monitor, sold as one SKU: Vatrer 48V 105Ah Club Car Lithium Battery kit. Vatrer says it is designed for 48V Club Car DS, Precedent, Tempo and Onward (19.69 × 12.52 × 9.6 in case) and comes with its dedicated charger, LCD monitor, mounting bracket and install accessories. One SKU, so one cart.
Alternative for EZGO owners: Vatrer 48V 105Ah EZGO kit. Vatrer lists TXT, RXV, Medalist, Marathon, 2Five and Express 4x4, with a 58.4V 18A lithium charger included. Same price as the Club Car kit.

Lower-price alternative: Redodo 48V (51.2V) 100Ah Bluetooth conversion kit (battery + 58.4V 18A charger + 500A shunt monitor). Redodo lists it for Club Car, EZGO, ICON and Yamaha, as a replacement for 6× 8V or 8× 6V lead-acid batteries.

Club Car OBC bypass (wiring step, or a Lester-type bypass kit that no approved store sells): needed on Club Cars that still have the On-Board Computer, or the new lithium charger won't run properly. I couldn't confirm that either kit includes it.
Exclusion: don't build 48V from four Redodo 12V 100Ah Group 24 packs. Redodo's own page says they are NOT suitable as a golf cart battery.

findings.label: OBC blocks a non-OEM charger
findings.value: On 2006-and-newer Club Car models the attached non-OEM charger 'will not be able to recognize the voltage' and won't start; on older models the charger 'will become a slave to the OBC'
findings.source_title: Why and How to Bypass the Club Car Onboard Computer (ImpactBattery, 2016-12-08)
findings.note: This is a battery retailer's blog, not Club Car. It says Club Car fitted OBCs on 48V carts 'as early as 1995'. The bypass it describes: a 12-gauge wire from pack negative to the black-wire terminal on the back of the charge receptacle. It does not mention lithium.
